_comment: Showcase scene script. Each scene defines what the LEFT and RIGHT panels show, plus a caption that's the analytical takeaway. Layers reference GeoJSON files in geojson/ relative to the project root.

scenes.title: The atlanta food system, in two lenses
Where you live decides what you eat
scenes.caption: North Atlanta concentrates wealth, education, and grocery access. South & West Atlanta carries the opposite. The income gradient (left) maps cleanly onto the food-desert gradient (right) — segregation patterns from redlining still drive food access today.

scenes.title: Two grocery atlantas
scenes.caption: Grocery retail clusters in Buckhead and Midtown. Convenience stores and fast-food chains fill the void in South-side neighborhoods. The same surface, two food economies.

scenes.title: Transit-served vs car-dependent
scenes.caption: MARTA rail (left) is mostly North-South. Bus coverage exists but is infrequent, and roughly half of South Atlanta tracts sit beyond a 30-minute transit ride to a grocery store (right).

scenes.title: The body keeps the score
scenes.caption: Obesity prevalence (left, CDC PLACES) shadows lived food insecurity (right, CDC PLACES). Both indicators follow the same north-rich / south-poor gradient — the structural USDA food-desert flag is one explanation, but obesity and food insecurity track even tracts that LILA doesn't formally flag.

scenes.title: Where the body and the map agree
scenes.caption: Bivariate choropleth — obesity prevalence (3 tertiles) × USDA LILA-strictness (3 classes). Tracts in the deep-clay corner are simultaneously food-deserts AND high-obesity — the cluster where AFCN intervention should focus first. Method: Stevens (2015), 'Bivariate Choropleth Maps'. 528 tracts joined on GEOID; 20 fall into the high/strict cell.

right.title: AFCN orgs on the bivariate base

scenes.title: Who's already on the ground
scenes.caption: AFCN's curated directory of 802 organizations. Left: physical points where work happens. Right: which categories of work concentrate where — pantries congregate in lower-income tracts, urban farms cluster in Westside neighborhoods.

scenes.title: Georgia tech as a campus-to-community pump
scenes.caption: Zooming to GT campus, dining halls in green produce 2,316 lbs of weekly surplus while neighboring food pantries (red points beyond campus) operate in deficit. The campus is the closest, fastest, freshest recovery source most pantries are not yet plugged into.

scenes.title: How atlanta is zoned
scenes.caption: City of Atlanta zoning across 2,967 polygons. Residential dominates the northside (warm tans), commercial corridors thread through Buckhead and Midtown (clay), industrial concentrates near the airport and rail (slate), and SPI overlays mark the BeltLine special-interest districts (deep clay).
scenes.insight: City of Atlanta DPCD · 2,967 zoning polygons

scenes.title: Five atlantas, one matrix
scenes.caption: Synthesis: every tract classified into one of five urban typologies. High-growth Core (BeltLine), Affluent Suburban (North), Disinvested Urban (S/W), Industrial Logistics (near airport), Emerging Mixed-use (BeltLine edges). The matrix's punchline.
